newsitem.title: USA: Perry says expects Bosnia follow-on decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Perry says expects Bosnia follow-on decision soon.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Perry said on Thursday that he expected President Bill Clinton to decide soon on possible U.S. participation in any follow-on peacekeeping force for Bosnia to replace the U.S.-led force scheduled to wind up its mission next month.

Perry told reporters Clinton was considering four options laid down by NATO military planners, three of which involve some form of a follow-on force, "and I'm expecting a decision from the president in the near future." He declined to confirm reports that Vice President Al Gore had already signaled to NATO a U.S. willingness to join a follow-on force.
Perry said he did not want to forecast exactly when Clinton would make up his mind "nor would I want to forecast what his decision would be."
He made his comments during a picture-taking session with visiting Defense Minister Severin Adjori of the West African state of Benin.

The Washington Post and the New York Times reported earlier on Thursday that the administration's reported willingness to participate in a new peacekeeping force had been communicated by Gore on Wednesday to NATO Secretary General Javier Solona.

The Post quoted senior NATO officials as saying the potential new force would number up to 30,000 troops, including 5,000 to 10,000 Americans, and likely would remain in Bosnia until the end of next year.
